map.Unit 3 · Episode 3 — the international q: Unit 3 · Episode 3 — the world qualifier race. The Courier Cup needs an OK course. Three gates stand in the way. Solve the math to move the story.
Glitch check: the qualifier route. The units are… fighting. Reader, get set.
map.Previously, in Episode 2: ratio tables s: Last time, in Episode 2: ratio tables scaled the aid stops for each heat. One honest graph broke Team Torque's "record" stats. Their points bent off the line. Now the world qualifier comes to Axiom City. Its route signs use five different units.
Riders from four lands come at noon. Their route cards use miles and inches. Half my signs are metric. Make it all match by nine. If not, the qualifier is OFF.
A unit side quest before the main race. Kofi, team up?
map.Co-op. First fact for the record: the co: Team up. First fact: the course never changes. Only its labels do.
map.Confirmed. A conversion is just a ratio: Yes. A conversion is just a ratio in a coat.
map.The staging tent, 6:40 a.m. Chloe stenci: The tent, 6:40 a.m. Chloe paints blank signs. Rohan rolls the wheel in circles. It clicks. He loves it.
map.Watch one: the connector sign says 0.8 k: Watch this one. The sign says 0.8 km. Meters are smaller, so the count grows: 0.8 × 1000 = 800 m. Same path, new name.
map.The wheel agrees. One click per meter. E: The wheel agrees. One click per meter. Eight hundred clicks of pure joy.
map.Metric rule, archived: every step is a p: Metric rule: each step is a power of ten. 1 m = 100 cm. 1 kg = 1000 g. And always: bigger unit, smaller number.
map.Converting within a system means trading: Converting within a system: you swap one unit for a new one. Both are in the SAME group. Multiply or divide by 10, 100, or 1000.
map.Reader — two crooked signs left. Re-labe: Reader, two wrong signs are left. Fix their labels before the marshal melts.
map.Two signs still lie. Sign A marks the fi: Two signs are still wrong. Sign A says the finish chute is 5.5 m. But it should be in centimeters. Sign B says the ice is 4500 g. But the sheet wants kilograms. Fix both labels.
map.Conceptual: a conversion never changes t: Conceptual: a conversion never changes the chute or the ice. Only the unit changes. Go DOWN to a smaller unit? Then you get MORE of them (multiply). Go UP to a bigger unit? Then you get FEWER (divide).
map.Procedural: centi- is the ×100 step (1 m: Procedural: centi- is the ×100 step (1 m = 100 cm). Kilo- is the ×1000 jump (1 kg = 1000 g). Sign A: multiply by 100. Sign B: divide by 1000.
map.My bridge chart. Two facts. Guard them w: My bridge chart. Two facts. Guard them well.
map.Watch one more: the 4 km connector in mi: Watch one more. The 4 km path in miles: 4 ÷ 1.6 = 2.5 mi. Fewer miles than kilometers. Each mile is longer.
map.And tiny stuff works the same: a 2-inch: Small things work the same. A 2-inch number plate is 2 × 2.54 = 5.08 cm. Centimeters are shorter, so the count grows. Check the way you go each time.
map.Converting between systems uses a bridge: Converting between systems uses a bridge ratio. It is a fact like 1 mi ≈ 1.6 km. It names one unit with the other. Then multiply or divide. Check which way you go.
map.Reader, take the chart. The big loop and: Reader, take the chart. Take the big loop and the sticker strip across.
map.The marshal's chart: 1 mi ≈ 1.6 km · 1 i: The marshal's chart: 1 mi ≈ 1.6 km · 1 in = 2.54 cm. Two route cards are left. Put the 12 km loop in miles. Put a 5-inch sticker strip in centimeters.
map.Conceptual: between systems you need a b: Conceptual: between systems, you need a bridge ratio. It names ONE unit with the other. Then it is the same game. Longer unit, fewer of them. Shorter unit, more of them.
map.Procedural: km → miles crosses the 1.6 b: Procedural: km → miles: cross the 1.6 bridge by DIVISION. Each mile holds 1.6 km of road. Inches → centimeters: cross the 2.54 bridge by MULTIPLICATION. Each inch is worth 2.54 cm.
map.8:15 a.m. Forty signboards, one stencil,: 8:15 a.m. Forty signs. One stencil. Two systems. No room to slip.
map.Every sign gets BOTH labels now. Could I: Each sign gets BOTH labels now. Could I make them smell like churros? Yes. Did the marshal let me? No.
map.Rohan and Kofi run the numbers, Chloe pa: Rohan and Kofi do the numbers. Chloe paints. I check the list. The crew is at full speed.
map.Distortion fading… except at the marshal: The glitch fades. But not at the marshal's desk. Something on a clipboard will go wrong on purpose.
map.8:40 a.m. The marshal's desk. Team Torqu: 8:40 a.m. The marshal's desk. Team Torque shows up. Same jackets. One complaint.
map.Your \"total course\" is a scramble of m: Your "total course" mixes miles and kilometers. I say it does not add up. If not by nine, nobody races.
map.It adds up fine. You just have to put ev: It adds up fine. Put each leg in the same units. Then add. That is the whole rule.
map.Final boss just announced itself. Certif: The last boss is here. A form with two blanks and one trick question.
map.Adding 2 and 3.2 while their units disag: Adding 2 and 3.2 when the units are not the same? That would be… a glitch. Convert first. Add second.
map.8:55 a.m. The form that decides everythi: 8:55 a.m. This form decides it all. The marshal opens the pen.
map.Easy out for you all: everyone knows 1 k: Here is an easy way out. All know 1 kilometer is longer than 1 mile. Write that down. See what happens.
map.The form takes true statements only. Cre: The form takes true facts only. Crew and reader, finish it.
map.BOSS GATE. Three locks. The qualifier —: BOSS GATE. Three locks. The qualifier rides on your conversions. So does Torque's smug face.
map.Boss fight, reader. You carry the chart,: Boss fight, reader. You carry the chart. I will carry the pens.
map.The certification form. The course = a 2: The form. The course = a 2-mile leg plus a 3.2 km leg. Chart: 1 mi ≈ 1.6 km. Three locks:
map.The Torque captain's claim — \"1 kilomet: The Torque captain says: "1 kilometer is longer than 1 mile". True or false?
map.Conceptual: you can only ADD lengths tha: Conceptual: you can only ADD lengths with the SAME unit. Convert first. Add second. Then kilometers to meters is a within-system step: the ×1000 jump.
map.Procedural: Lock 1 — turn the 2-mile leg: Procedural: Lock 1: make the 2-mile leg into kilometers (each mile ≈ 1.6 km). Then add the 3.2. Lock 2: take your Lock 1 total from km → m. Lock 3: read the bridge fact again. If 1 mile ≈ 1.6 km, which unit is longer?
map.Certified — every sign, both systems, on: Approved. Each sign, both systems, one honest course. Complaint thrown out. The heats run at noon.
map.For the record: the captain's \"easy out: And note: the captain's "easy out" was 0.6 kilometers off.
map.Side quest complete. Main quest: the Cou: Side quest done. Main quest: the Courier Cup. Prize: one library.
map.New distortion at the start line. It's f: A new glitch is at the start line. It is fast. To be continued…
map.Within a system.Trade units in the same: Within a system.Trade units in one group by powers of ten: 1 m = 100 cm, 1 kg = 1000 g. Big unit, small count. Small unit, big count.
map.Between systems.Cross on a bridge ratio:: Between systems.Cross on a bridge ratio: 1 mi ≈ 1.6 km, 1 in = 2.54 cm. Multiply or divide by the bridge number.
map.The direction check.Before you accept an: The direction check.Look at your answer. Should the count get big or get small? Longer unit, fewer of them.
map.Across the line.A distance never changes: Across the line.A distance does not change when its name does. Units are ratios. Convert first. Add second.
map.completed Unit 3 · Episode 3: Across the: beat Unit 3 · Episode 3: Across the Line. They can convert units. They can do it in one system. And they can do it between two.
map.A banner crew re-labels a 3.2 m banner i: A crew puts a 3.2 m banner in centimeters. Smaller unit, bigger count: 3.2 × 100 = 320 cm.
map.A water crate weighs 7000 g and the shee: A crate of water is 7000 g. The sheet wants kilograms. Bigger unit, smaller count: 7000 ÷ 1000 = 7 kg.
map.Direction check both times: the number G: Check the way it went: the number GREW going m → cm. It SHRANK going g → kg. The banner and the water did not change.
map.Your turn — same idea, different numbers: Your turn. Same idea, new numbers:
map.The 8 km river leg in miles: 8 ÷ 1.6 = 8: The 8 km river leg in miles: 8 ÷ 1.6 = 80 ÷ 16 = 5 miles. Fewer miles than kilometers. That is the right way.
map.A 3-inch decal in centimeters: 3 × 2.54: A 3-inch sticker in centimeters: 3 × 2.54 = 7.62 cm. More centimeters than inches. Right again.
map.Two bridges, one rule: write the ratio,: Two bridges, one rule. Write the ratio. Pick the way to go. Then multiply or divide.
map.A 10-inch pennant is how many centimeter: A 10-inch flag is how many centimeters?
map.A practice course: a 3-mile flat leg plu: A test course: a 3-mile flat leg plus a 1.2 km bridge leg.
map.Same units first: 3 × 1.6 = 4.8 km. Now: Same units first: 3 × 1.6 = 4.8 km. Now add: 4.8 + 1.2 = 6 km.
map.The form wants meters too: 6 × 1000 = 60: The form wants meters too: 6 × 1000 = 6000 m. Convert, add, then step within the system.
map.A 1-mile leg plus a 2.4 km leg — total i: A 1-mile leg plus a 2.4 km leg. Total in kilometers?
map.Sign A holds. ×1000 is the KILO jump (km: Sign A is wrong. ×1000 is the KILO jump (km ↔ m, kg ↔ g). Meters to CENTImeters is the ×100 step.
map.Sign A holds. Direction check: a centime: Sign A is wrong. Check the way: a centimeter is SMALLER than a meter. So the count must get BIGGER. Multiply.
map.Sign A holds. How many centimeters make: Sign A is wrong. How many centimeters make one meter? Scale 5.5 by just that.
map.Sign B holds. ÷100 belongs to the meter–: Sign B is wrong. ÷100 goes with the meter–centimeter step. Grams to KILOgrams is the ÷1000 jump.
map.Sign B holds. Direction check: a kilogra: Sign B is wrong. Check the way: a kilogram is the BIGGER unit. So the count must get SMALLER. Divide.
map.Sign B holds. 'Kilo' means 1000 — how ma: Sign B is wrong. 'Kilo' means 1000. How many grams make one kilogram?
map.550 cm and 4.5 kg — 5.5 × 100 and 4500 ÷: 550 cm and 4.5 kg: 5.5 × 100 and 4500 ÷ 1000. Same chute, same ice, honest labels. Chloe's stencil hisses. It is glad.
map.Card 1 holds. You went the long way — a: Card 1 is wrong. You went the wrong way. A mile is LONGER than a kilometer. So the loop has FEWER miles. Divide by 1.6.
map.Card 1 holds. How many groups of 1.6 km: Card 1 is wrong. How many 1.6 km groups fit in the 12 km loop?
map.Card 2 holds. Wrong direction — a centim: Card 2 is wrong. Wrong way. A centimeter is SHORTER than an inch. So the strip has MORE centimeters. Multiply by 2.54.
map.Card 2 holds. Each of the 5 inches is wo: Card 2 is wrong. Each of the 5 inches is worth just 2.54 cm. Scale it.
12 ÷ 1.6 = 7.5 miles, and 5 × 2.54 = 12.7 cm. The riders' cards now match the city's signs. Bridge crossed.
map.Lock 1 holds. 2 + 3.2 adds miles straigh: Lock 1 is shut. 2 + 3.2 adds miles right to kilometers. Units that do not match can't be added. Convert the 2-mile leg to km FIRST.
map.Lock 1 holds. Each mile of the harbor le: Lock 1 is shut. Each mile of the harbor leg is about 1.6 km. Convert it. THEN add the 3.2 km climb.
map.Lock 2 holds. That's the ×100 step — but: Lock 2 is shut. That is the ×100 step. But 'kilo' means 1000. 1 km = 1000 m.
map.Lock 2 holds. Sanity check: meters are s: Lock 2 is shut. Check: meters are smaller than kilometers. So the count must GROW. Take your Lock 1 total ×1000.
map.Lock 3 holds. Sanity-check it against th: Lock 3 is shut. Check the chart. It takes 1.6 km to make ONE mile. That is more than a whole kilometer. So which unit is longer?
map.CERTIFIED. 2 × 1.6 + 3.2 = 6.4 km = 6400: CERTIFIED. 2 × 1.6 + 3.2 = 6.4 km = 6400 m. And the mile is still the longer unit. The marshal stamps the form. ACROSS THE LINE!
Yes! Now go back and open that gate.
